attrs.evidence: World row L-COORD-2 (4/4): an in-pass defs.set refuses and leaves no GHOST in defs or in the after-map; an in-pass cross-node state.set refuses and the receipt's warrant_id now comes from the publication and equals the world's; a caller-owned spec retained across registration is severed and the pass derives honestly with the stored spec frozen against assignment; and poisoning from OUTSIDE a pass still works — the seam L-MAINT-3/L-MAINT-5 depend on — with the snapshot reporting coordinator_diverged rather than preferring a side. All three attack witnesses are frozen RED against World 0.8.0 in probe_coordinator_alias_9d1_repro.mjs, where they reproduced 0/3 confined. grid_check v2.15 scans for the guard constructs; three negative cases die on distinct diagnostics.
attrs.statement: Once a maintenance pass begins, every semantic input governing it — definitions, derivation bindings, dependency topology and coordinator state — is immutable for the duration of the transaction, and no RETAINED ALIAS may mutate those inputs outside the coordinator's guarded transition API. Sealing the coordinator's properties is insufficient: a frozen property still points at a mutable Map, and a registration that stores the caller's spec by reference leaves authoritative configuration in the caller's hands. Writes go through stores that consult the in-flight flag, values are owned and frozen on the way in, and the pass computes against a definition view captured at entry. Separately, a receipt may not assemble one apparently authoritative fact out of two independent sources: publication fields come from the publication, coordinator state is compared against it, and disagreement is DECLARED.
